message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to live air‑quality feeds, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment.  

**What you can do instead:**

| Source | How to use it | Typical data shown |
|--------|---------------|--------------------|
| **AirNow.gov** | Go to the site, enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code, and click “Get AQI.” | Current AQI, pollutant breakdown (PM₂.₅, O₃, NO₂, etc.), forecast for the next 48 h |
| **EPA Air Quality Index app** | Download the free app for iOS/Android, set Los Angeles as your location. | Real‑time AQI, health recommendations, alerts |
| **Local news sites** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | Check their weather/air‑quality sections. | Often include a quick snapshot of the AQI and any alerts |
| **Weather apps** (e.g., Weather.com, AccuWeather) | Look for the “Air Quality” tab. | Current AQI, pollutant levels, forecast |

**Typical LA air‑quality pattern (for context):**

- **Spring & early summer:** Ozone levels often rise due to sunny, stagnant conditions, especially on weekends.  
- **Fall & winter:** PM₂.₅ can spike from wild‑fire smoke or residential heating.  
- **Overall trend:** Los Angeles usually stays in the “Moderate” (AQI 51–100) range most days, but occasional “Unhealthy” (AQI 151–200) episodes can occur during wildfire season or high‑ozone days.

If you need the current AQI right now, the quickest way is to check one of the sources above. Let me know if you’d like a quick guide on interpreting the AQI numbers or how to protect yourself on high‑pollution days!
